NetSat (blind test): telemetry recovered from orbital physics

Every field below was found without a decoder: candidate byte readings were tested against sunlight, thermal lag, orbital phase, wall-clock time and the IGRF magnetic field computed from the TLE. Names, units and scales are Claude's reading of that evidence, with the satellite name withheld.

Frame type raw:len89

1724 frames, 241 passes, 89-byte payload

Every frame was heard in sunlight, but many came minutes after an eclipse (the shadow falls where there are no ground stations): sunlight history still separates the fields.

An 89-byte beacon with several rolling counters and many fields that all move together with the same sunlight-history trend. The candidate fields look like a mixed block of housekeeping or counter data. The strong common correlation is probably a time or phase artifact (long-term drift or reboot epochs) rather than real physics for each field.

Health. Not enough evidence for battery or thermal health, because no field can be confidently identified as a voltage or temperature. The counters show 10 resets in the window, the last about 60 days before the end, which suggests repeated reboots or wraps, but this is uncertain. All frames are in sunlight, so there is no shadow contrast.

Frame type raw:len68

938 frames, 237 passes, 68-byte payload

Every frame was heard in sunlight, but many came minutes after an eclipse (the shadow falls where there are no ground stations): sunlight history still separates the fields.

A 68-byte beacon frame with two monotonically increasing counters found, and no sensor fields detected. Both counters grow at about 0.11 per second, roughly one count per 9 s, and show no dependence on sunlight or beta angle.

Health. Not enough evidence for battery or thermal health, since no such fields were found. The u2le counter at offset 22 reset 3 times in 150 days, most recently 12.5 days before the end of the window. That points to occasional reboots, but they might instead be deliberate counter resets.

frame_sequence_counter [counts]

byte 22 · u2le · counter · counter
score 0.99 · per s 0.108 · rough 0.007
raw · confidence 0.60

u2le that rises in 99% of in-pass steps at 0.108/s, with no sun or beta correlation. It wrapped or reset 3 times in 150 days, the last 12.5 days before the end, so it may be an uptime or frame counter that reboots, or a 16-bit value that is reset rarely. It has not reached 65535, so these are not simple wraps.

frame_counter_low_byte [counts]

byte 62 · s1 · counter · counter
score 0.98 · per s 0.111 · rough 0.144
raw + 128 (unsigned wrap) · confidence 0.40

s1 that increases at 0.111/s, in step with the counter at offset 22, and wraps 11 times in a pass, which fits a signed byte used as a rolling sequence number. The 36 resets are mostly 8-bit wraps by design, so it is not a reliable reboot indicator.
